title: PRD: Budgeted Rollout Orchestrator
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This PRD describes the Budgeted Rollout Orchestrator (BRO) — a service and UX layer that enables controlled feature and model variant rollouts constrained by an explicit cost budget and SLO budget. BRO coordinates staged releases across tenant cohorts while ensuring rollout spend stays within pre-approved credit envelopes and maintaining end-user latency/availability SLOs.

Why this exists

- Customers and internal product teams have asked for safer ways to roll out expensive variants (higher-fidelity models, larger context windows, or non-quantized kernels) without surprising bill spikes.
- Existing canary tooling manages traffic percentages but does not reason about dollar or token budgets, nor does it automatically stop or adapt a rollout when cost signals or SLO regressions appear.

Goals (measurable)

1. Prevent per-release overspend: 95% of rollouts must not exceed the configured budget envelope more than 2% across a 30-day window.
2. SLO first: BRO must detect SLO degradation (latency P95 or error rate) and halt or roll back within 5 minutes of breach detection for 90% of incidents.
3. Developer UX: expose a rollout API and console that lets teams define budget envelopes, sampling policies, and automatic remediation in < 10 minutes.
4. Integration: produce billing hooks for forecasting and a reconciliation report for Finance within 24 hours of rollout completion.

Non-goals

- BRO will not replace low-level model serving routing (the runtime continues to serve traffic). It orchestrates routing policies and budgets.
- BRO will not perform chargeback accounting at the token level; that remains in billing pipelines. BRO emits reconciliation artifacts to be consumed by billing.

User personas

- Product Engineer: wants to release a new high-fidelity variant to 10% of users with a $2,000 rollout budget and automatic stop on latency regressions.
- Platform Engineer: integrates BRO with CI to attach rollout policies to releases.
- Finance / Commercial: consumes reconciliation reports to validate credits and customer notifications.

Core user journeys

1. Create rollout (console/API): select model variant, set budget envelope (currency or token cap), SLO thresholds (P95 latency, error rate), cohort selection (by tenant tag or percentage), and remediation policy (pause, rollback, reduce fidelity).
2. Monitor: BRO shows live spend consumption, SLO health, and projected time-to-budget exhaustion.
3. Auto-remediate: BRO executes remediation when thresholds cross. An audit/log is emitted for every action.

Functional requirements

- FR-1: Budget types — Support monetary budget (USD), token budget, and a hybrid budget (USD + token heuristic).
- FR-2: SLO bindings — Accept SLO definitions: latency P50/P95/P99, request error-rate %, and custom telemetry signals (from Console).
- FR-3: Cohort definitions — Cohorts can be defined as: tenant list, percent-of-traffic, header-anchored sampling, or experiment cohort ID.
- FR-4: Policy language — A simple DSL to express triggers and actions, e.g.:

  when budget_consumed >= 80% and p95_latency >= baseline * 1.25 then reduce_traffic_by(50%)

- FR-5: Forecasting — Provide projected budget curve and ETA to exhaustion using live sampled consumption rates (windowed by 1/5/15 minutes).
- FR-6: Auditing and reconciliation — Emit daily & per-release artifacts: rollout_log.json, spend_snapshot.csv, and reconciliation_summary.txt to S3 for billing and review.
- FR-7: Integrations — Hooks for: Billing (forecast + final), Optimize (suggested batch/quant changes when budgets are tight), Console (UI for creation/monitoring), and CI/CD (API/CLI to attach policy to release).

Non-functional requirements

- NFR-1: Latency for decisioning pipeline must be <= 30s from telemetry ingestion to policy action.
- NFR-2: Availability SLA for BRO control-plane: 99.95% monthly. Fail-open defaults to safe minimal traffic (no automatic promotion) if BRO is unreachable.
- NFR-3: Data retention: keep rollout audit artifacts for 13 months; reconciliation artifacts for 25 months.

Success metrics (OKRs)

- O1: Reduce unexpected billing escalations tied to rollouts by 80% in first 6 months.
- O2: 90% of rollouts complete within configured budgets when the policy is used.

High-level architecture

Components:
- BRO API Service (control plane): receives rollout definitions, validates policies, and exposes API/console endpoints.
- Decision Engine: rule evaluator that ingests telemetry (SLO metrics, token usage) and evaluates DSL policies.
- Watcher Agents: lightweight readers that subscribe to serving runtime telemetry (via streaming topics) and surface per-cohort aggregates.
- Action Dispatcher: executes remediation by calling Runtime Routing API (adjust weights) and optional Optimize API (apply quantization or batching suggestions).
- Audit & Reconciliation Store: S3-backed export & a metadata index in Postgres for search/query.

Sequence of actions (simplified):
1) Product creates rollout via BRO API. BRO validates budget and cohort.
2) BRO registers cohort with Watcher Agents and starts consumption tracking.
3) Decision Engine evaluates DSL every 30s; when a rule fires Action Dispatcher calls the runtime routing API.
4) BRO writes audit event and pushes reconciliation artifacts upon completion or on schedule.

Security & Compliance

- All API calls authenticated with short-lived tokens (OIDC).
- Sensitive reconciliation artifacts (containing customer IDs and spend) are encrypted at rest (SSE-KMS) and access-controlled to Finance and Security.
- Access to create rollouts is gated by RBAC: only members of teams with the 'rollout:create' permission can create budgets > $1,000.

Operational runbook (initial)

1. Incident: BRO fails to take action but runtime continues serving expensive variant.
   - Pager duty: on-call BRO engineer.
   - Immediate mitigation: CLI to trigger global safety action (force-reduce-traffic 100%).
   - Postmortem: capture root cause, update playbooks.
2. Reconciliation mismatch (billing vs BRO artifacts):
   - Triage: Finance and BRO owner triage within 48 hours using reconciliation_summary.txt.

Rollout plan (MVP -> Beta -> GA)

- MVP (Q4 2026): Budgeted rollouts with monetary envelope, percent-based cohorts, simple stop/rollback actions, decisioning every 60s, console view with live spend and SLO indicators.
- Beta (Q1 2027): Token budgets, DSL policy editor, forecasting curves, integrations with Optimize suggestions, faster decisioning (30s).
- GA (Q2 2027): Full billing hooks, reconciliation automations, CI/CD integrations, RBAC enforcement and SLAs.

Console & API examples

- Example API payload to create rollout:

  POST /v1/rollouts
  {
    "name": "hf-variant-2026-09",
    "model_variant": "gptx-variant-large",
    "cohort": {"percent": 10},
    "budget": {"type": "usd", "limit": 2000},
    "slo": {"p95_latency_ms": 250, "error_rate_pct": 0.5},
    "policy": "when budget_consumed >= 80% then reduce_traffic_by(50%)\nwhen p95_latency >= 250 then rollback()"
  }

- Sample rollout log entry (one-line JSON):

  2026-09-15T14:03:20Z | rollout_id=1234 | event=reduce_traffic | action_by=BRO | details=\"reduced to 5% due to budget: 82%\"

Open questions (for Product/Finance/Legal)

- Q1: What are acceptable default budgets for internal dogfooding?
- Q2: How should credits be displayed to end-customers if rollouts trigger commercial credits?
- Q3: Do we need per-tenant opt-in for automatic rollback actions that temporarily reduce fidelity?

Appendix: Sample DSL grammar (informal)

- trigger := metric comparator value
- metric := budget_consumed | p95_latency | error_rate | custom
- comparator := >= | > | <= | < | ==
- action := reduce_traffic_by(percent) | rollback() | notify(team) | apply_optimize_suggestion(id)

Appendix: Example reconciliation CSV columns

- rollout_id, cohort, start_ts, end_ts, budget_type, budget_limit, spend_usd, tokens_consumed, actions_taken, final_state

Dependencies & cross-team owners

- Runtime Routing API (eng-serving-runtime) — owner: Runtime team (integration contract required).
- Billing export / forecast (finance-and-legal) — owner: Finance.
- Optimize suggestion API (eng-optimize) — owner: Optimize/Research.
- Console UI surface (eng-developer-experience) — owner: DevX.

Next steps (30 days)

1. Align on policy DSL minimal feature set (Product + Runtime + Finance).
2. Prototype Decision Engine evaluating budget and p95 signals over synthetic telemetry.
3. Design console wireframes for create/monitor flow with DevX.
